- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates, layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
## What happened

On `modernize-macos26` you have two commits past `master`:
- `76c5ffd` — removed Sparkle.framework
- `50117e5` — **removed the `Dependencies/PXSourceList` git submodule** (deleted the submodule entry and the `.gitmodules` line)

That last commit pulled out the library but nothing replaced it, and the app still depends on PXSourceList in three places, so the build can't resolve it:

1. **Source code** — the whole sidebar is built on it:
   - [BPSideBarController.h](Cakebrew/Controllers/BPSideBarController.h) — `@import PXSourceList;`, conforms to `PXSourceListDataSource`/`PXSourceListDelegate`, `IBOutlet PXSourceList *sidebar`
   - [BPSideBarController.m](Cakebrew/Controllers/BPSideBarController.m) — uses `PXSourceListItem`, `PXSourceListTableCellView` throughout
   - [BPHomebrewViewController.h:23](Cakebrew/Controllers/BPHomebrewViewController.h:23) — `#import <PXSourceList/PXSourceList.h>`
2. **Xcode project** — [project.pbxproj](Cakebrew.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj) still links & copies `PXSourceList.framework` and sets `USER_HEADER_SEARCH_PATHS` to its headers. The framework was built from the submodule, which is now gone.
3. **The XIB** — [MainMenu.xib:952](Cakebrew/Base.lproj/MainMenu.xib:952) sets the sidebar's `customClass="PXSourceList"`, with cells `PXSourceListTableCellView` and a `PXSourceListBadgeView`.

So this wasn't an accident in the usual sense — the submodule was deliberately removed, but the migration off PXSourceList was never done.

## Two ways forward

The good news: PXSourceList is just an old wrapper around `NSOutlineView` to get the "source list" sidebar look. Modern AppKit does that natively — your XIB already has `selectionHighlightStyle="sourceList"` and a `_sourceListBackgroundColor`. So you don't need the library anymore.

Let me ask which direction you want before I touch anything.

Screen capture is blocked (Terminal lacks Screen Recording permission), so I can't grab a visual. I'll be straight about that: I verified the build and a clean, crash-free launch, but I could not visually confirm the sidebar's appearance — the app is running now so you can eyeball it.

Here's where things stand.

## What was broken
Commit `50117e5` removed the `Dependencies/PXSourceList` submodule, but four things still depended on it, so nothing could build:
- The **workspace** ([contents.xcworkspacedata](Cakebrew.xcworkspace/contents.xcworkspacedata)) still referenced the now-missing `PXSourceList.xcodeproj` — this alone breaks the whole workspace.
- The **project** linked, copied, and header-searched `PXSourceList.framework`.
- The **source** (`BPSideBarController`, `BPHomebrewViewController.h`) used PXSourceList classes/protocols.
- The **XIB** set the sidebar and its cells to PXSourceList custom classes.

## What I changed (migrated to native `NSOutlineView`)
- [BPSideBarController.h](Cakebrew/Controllers/BPSideBarController.h) / [.m](Cakebrew/Controllers/BPSideBarController.m) — dropped `@import PXSourceList`; now conform to `NSOutlineViewDataSource/Delegate`. Added small native replacements: `BPSidebarItem` (model), `BPSidebarTableCellView` (cell with a badge outlet), and `BPSidebarBadgeView` (draws the count pill, with selected/normal styling). Group rows use `isGroupItem:` and are kept expanded (`shouldCollapseItem:` → NO) so the existing flat `FormulaeSideBarItem` row indices still line up.
- [BPHomebrewViewController.h](Cakebrew/Controllers/BPHomebrewViewController.h) — removed the PXSourceList import.
- [MainMenu.xib](Cakebrew/Base.lproj/MainMenu.xib) — outline view is now a stock `NSOutlineView` (it already had `selectionHighlightStyle="sourceList"`); cells point at the new classes.
- [project.pbxproj](Cakebrew.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj) and the workspace — removed all PXSourceList framework/project references.

No new files were added — the three helper classes live in the sidebar controller, so the only project edits were removals.

## Verification
- `xcodebuild ... -workspace Cakebrew.xcworkspace -scheme Cakebrew` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED** (both app and tests).
- App launches and stays running; no exceptions in the unified log.
- **Not verified visually** — please confirm the sidebar looks right (group headers "Formulae"/"Tools", icons, and the count badges, especially a selected row's badge).

One leftover: `Credits.rtf` still credits PXSourceList in the acknowledgements — harmless to the build, but stale now.

## Summary
- Removes the **Sparkle.framework** vendored binary and fixes acknowledgements URL handling.
- Removes the **PXSourceList** git submodule.
- Migrates the sidebar from PXSourceList to a **native `NSOutlineView`** source list, which restores the build:
  - Adds lightweight `BPSidebarItem` (model), `BPSidebarTableCellView` (cell), and `BPSidebarBadgeView` (count pill) classes in `BPSideBarController`.
  - Reimplements the data source/delegate against `NSOutlineView`; group rows stay expanded so the existing `FormulaeSideBarItem` row indices still line up.
  - Drops all `PXSourceList.framework` references from `project.pbxproj` and the stale `PXSourceList.xcodeproj` ref from the workspace.

## Why
The PXSourceList submodule was removed earlier, but the code, Xcode project, and workspace still depended on it, so the app would not build. PXSourceList is just an old `NSOutlineView` wrapper; modern AppKit provides the source-list look natively.

## Test plan
- [x] `xcodebuild -workspace Cakebrew.xcworkspace -scheme Cakebrew` → BUILD SUCCEEDED (app + tests)
- [x] App launches and stays running; no exceptions in the unified log
- [ ] Visual check of the sidebar: group headers (Formulae / Tools), item icons, and count badges (including a selected row's badge)
- [ ] Confirm sidebar selection still drives the formula list correctly

## Follow-up
- `Credits.rtf` still lists PXSourceList in the acknowledgements (harmless to build, but now stale).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

Sparkle was fully removed from the Cakebrew app (the Sparkle.framework and its updater were deleted, and the "Check for Updates…" menu item was removed). However, the file Cakebrew/dsa_pub.pem — Sparkle's DSA public key used for verifying update signatures — is still bundled as an app resource and is now dead weight.

Please:
1. Delete the Cakebrew/dsa_pub.pem file.
2. Remove its references from Cakebrew.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj — there are two: a PBXBuildFile entry (id 15B23A2C18F5003600714212, "dsa_pub.pem in Resources") and a PBXFileReference (id 15B23A2B18F5003600714212), plus its entry in the Resources (PBXResourcesBuildPhase) files list and in whatever PBXGroup lists it.
3. Check Cakebrew/Cakebrew-Info.plist (and any other Info.plist) for leftover Sparkle keys (SUFeedURL, SUPublicDSAKeyFile, SUEnableAutomaticChecks, SUScheduledCheckInterval, etc.) and remove them.
4. Build with: xcodebuild -workspace Cakebrew.xcworkspace -scheme Cakebrew -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build — confirm BUILD SUCCEEDED.

Follow the repo's git workflow: do this on a branch, open a PR, and squash merge (do not commit to master directly).

I've now got the full picture, and **no — it's not ready yet.** The two finished tasks left things in a state that needs reconciling. Here's exactly what happened:

**1. The dsa-key removal (PR #2) merged into the wrong base.** That task opened PR #2 with base `modernize-macos26` instead of `master`, then squash-merged it there. So the dsa removal lives only on `modernize-macos26` — **`master` still has `dsa_pub.pem`** and the Sparkle Info.plist keys.

**2. The Credits cleanup is done but uncommitted** — the PXSourceList attribution is correctly removed from both `Credits.rtf` files (verified), but there's no commit, branch, or PR for it.

**3. `modernize-macos26` and `master` have diverged.** When PR #1 squash-merged, it created a fresh commit (`f755a5c`) on master. The old branch kept its original commits, so the two are now parallel histories. The *actual* content difference between them is small and clean though — exactly the remaining work:

content.text:
Here's your actual situation, confirmed from the API:

- **`scottdensmore/Cakebrew` is a fork** of `brunophilipe/Cakebrew` (that's the network root; the whole network has 257 repos).
- **Your fork has exactly one downstream fork:** `ruslan-khalitov/Cakebrew` — created Jan 2021, last pushed Jan 2021, so it's stale/inactive.

So your premise is correct: someone did fork your copy.

## What "leaving the fork network" actually involves

There's **no self-service button** to detach a fork. You have to **contact GitHub Support** and ask them to detach `scottdensmore/Cakebrew` into a standalone repository.

The downstream fork is the wrinkle you're sensing — but it's not necessarily a hard "no." GitHub's handling of this has changed over the years, and reports vary:
- Some people are told the fork can't be detached while it has its own forks, and to resolve those first.
- Others have Support detach it anyway and **re-parent** the downstream fork (it gets pointed at the next repo up the network, or becomes its own root).

I genuinely can't promise which applies to you today — GitHub's fork-detachment policy isn't publicly pinned down and shifts over time. **The reliable move is to open a GitHub Support ticket and ask directly**; they handle these case-by-case.

## The workaround that sidesteps all of this

If your real goal is "I want my repo to be a normal, independent project (no *forked from brunophilipe/Cakebrew* banner, indexed in search, PRs default to my repo)," you don't have to fight the detach process. You can create a brand-new repo and push your history into it:

1. Create a new **empty, non-fork** repo on GitHub (e.g. `scottdensmore/Cakebrew2` or a new name).
2. Mirror-push your code: `git push --mirror git@github.com:scottdensmore/<new>.git`
3. Point your local `origin` at the new repo.

That new repo is fully standalone, in no fork network, immediately. **Tradeoffs:** it won't carry over stars/watchers/issues/PRs, the URL changes, and your current fork (and its one downstream fork) keep existing untouched.

## Before you do anything — what's the goal?

The best path depends on *why* you want out of the network. Quick question:

content.text:
Here's what I found about how Cakebrew is actually built — it shapes what's worth doing:

- **Deployment target is `26.0`** (Tahoe-only) on the app + test targets. SDK is the latest (`macosx`), so you're already **building against the macOS 26 SDK** — that's what opts the app into Liquid Glass.
- **Window** is a custom `BPWindow` with a *classic* title bar (no `fullSizeContentView`, no unified toolbar style).
- **Sidebar/content use a classic `NSSplitView`** (thin divider) in the XIB — *not* the modern `NSSplitViewController` with a `.sidebar` split item. This is the single biggest thing standing between you and the signature Tahoe full-height translucent sidebar.
- **Toolbar** is a programmatic `NSToolbar` subclass (`BPToolbar`) with a plain `NSSearchField`, driven by `BPStyle`.
- Sidebar already uses **SF Symbols** (good start).

## On the minimum OS

You're currently Tahoe-only (26.0). "Last OS Apple still supports" = the current release minus two. With **Tahoe (26)** current, Apple ships security updates for **26, 15 (Sequoia), and 14 (Sonoma)** — so the floor is **macOS 14.0 Sonoma**.

Recommendation: set `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 14.0`. You'd still build against SDK 26, so it's **Liquid Glass on Tahoe, standard look on 14/15** — the normal way to do this. *(I'd want you to confirm the 14.0 target, and it comes with a small audit to guard any macOS 15/26-only APIs behind `@available`.)*

## What you already get free on Tahoe (SDK 26)
Toolbars, sheets, alerts, menus, standard controls, and the source-list sidebar already pick up the new materials/shapes just by building against SDK 26. The work below is about going from "auto-updated" to "looks intentional."

## Adoption features, by impact

**Tier 1 — signature Tahoe look (high impact)**
1. **Migrate to `NSSplitViewController` with a `.sidebar` split item** → full-height, translucent Liquid Glass sidebar that runs under the title bar. Biggest visual transformation. *(Larger change — restructures the window.)*
2. **Full-size content + unified toolbar**: `fullSizeContentView`, `titlebarAppearsTransparent`, `window.toolbarStyle = .unified`/`.unifiedCompact` so toolbar + title bar merge and float with glass.
3. **`NSTrackingSeparatorToolbarItem`** aligned to the split divider (the modern sidebar/content seam).

**Tier 2 — toolbar & controls**
4. **`NSSearchToolbarItem`** for search (proper expand/collapse + Tahoe styling) instead of the raw `NSSearchField`.
5. **Bordered toolbar items + SF Symbols** (`isBordered = YES`, symbol images, `NSToolbarItemGroup` for related actions).
6. **SF Symbols on buttons/empty states**, monochrome, matching Tahoe.

**Tier 3 — materials & polish**
7. **Audit hardcoded colors** (e.g., the sidebar header text color in the XIB) → swap for semantic `NSColor`s; verify dark mode.
8. **Revisit custom drawing** (`BPBackgroundView`, `BPStyle`) so it doesn't fight the glass; prefer `NSVisualEffectView` system materials.
9. **New layered app icon** via Icon Composer (`.icon`) — the rounded, glassy Tahoe icon. High visibility, self-contained.

Each tier is independently shippable as its own branch → PR (per your workflow). To scope this well:

input.prompt:
You are planning a UI modernization for an existing macOS app called **Cakebrew** (an Objective-C / AppKit GUI for Homebrew). The repo root is /Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/cakebrew. This is READ-ONLY research: produce a concrete implementation plan, do not edit files.

## Goal
Adopt the macOS 26 "Tahoe" (Liquid Glass) signature look for the main window. Specifically:
1. Convert the main window's sidebar+content from a classic `NSSplitView` to a modern **`NSSplitViewController`** where the sidebar is an `NSSplitViewItem` with `behavior = NSSplitViewItemBehaviorSidebar` (gives the full-height, translucent Liquid Glass sidebar that extends under the title bar).
2. Make the window use **full-size content** (`NSWindowStyleMaskFullSizeContentView`, `titlebarAppearsTransparent = YES`) and a **unified toolbar** (`window.toolbarStyle = NSWindowToolbarStyleUnified` or `…UnifiedCompact`).
3. Add an `NSTrackingSeparatorToolbarItem` aligned to the sidebar/content divider, if it fits the architecture.

The project already builds against the macOS 26 SDK with a minimum deployment target of macOS 14.0.

## What I already know about the architecture (verify and expand)
- The main UI is defined in `Cakebrew/Base.lproj/MainMenu.xib`.
- The window is `<window … id="371" customClass="BPWindow">` (a custom `NSWindow` subclass, `Cakebrew/BPWindow.{h,m}`), classic titled style mask (no fullSizeContentView today).
- There is a classic `<splitView dividerStyle="thin" id="hkt-Ff-Ha2">` holding: (a) a scrollView with a native `NSOutlineView` source-list sidebar driven by `BPSideBarController` (`Cakebrew/Controllers/BPSideBarController.{h,m}`), and (b) a content area with the formulae `NSScrollView`/table, an `NSTabView`, and info labels.
- The toolbar is a programmatic `NSToolbar` subclass `BPToolbar` (`Cakebrew/BPToolbar.{h,m}`), with items for update / info / search (`NSSearchField`) / multi-action. `BPStyle` (`Cakebrew/BPStyle.{h,m}`) supplies toolbar size etc.
- The main view controller is `BPHomebrewViewController` (`Cakebrew/Controllers/BPHomebrewViewController.{h,m}`); it has IBOutlets like `sidebarController`, `formulaeTableView`, `scrollView_formulae`, `tabView`. Its sidebar selection logic depends on FLAT outline-view row indices (a `FormulaeSideBarItem` enum 0..8) — this must keep working.

## What I need from you (the plan)
Investigate the actual files and produce a precise, low-risk migration plan that answers:
1. **Current wiring**: How is the window instantiated and shown? Is it loaded from MainMenu.xib as the app's main window (File's Owner = NSApplication / BPAppDelegate)? Is there a window controller or contentViewController today, or are views wired directly to the window's contentView? Trace how `BPHomebrewViewController` and `BPToolbar` get attached to the window (read `BPAppDelegate.m`, `BPHomebrewViewController.m`, `BPWindow.m`, and the relevant XIB connections).
2. **Migration approach**: Recommend whether to do the `NSSplitViewController` conversion in the XIB or programmatically (in code), given this is an old XIB-based app. Weigh the trade-offs. Identify the SAFEST path that preserves all existing IBOutlets/IBActions and the flat-row-index sidebar selection contract.
3. **Exact change list**: Enumerate the specific edits per file (which XIB objects/connections change, which code to add/modify, where to set `toolbarStyle`/`styleMask`/`titlebarAppearsTransparent`, where to create the split view controller and assign `behavior = sidebar`).
4. **Risks & gotchas**: e.g., how the sidebar's `selectRowIndexes:`/`selectedRow` usage in `BPHomebrewViewController.m` interacts with a sidebar split item; whether `BPWindow`/`BPStyle` custom drawing or hardcoded colors will fight the glass; auto-layout vs autoresizing-mask issues; how the toolbar attaches when moving to a contentViewController; minimum macOS 14 availability of every API you propose.
5. **Verification plan**: how to confirm it built and looks right (build command is `xcodebuild -workspace Cakebrew.xcworkspace -scheme Cakebrew -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build`; the app can be launched to eyeball the sidebar).

content.text:
The project builds against the macOS 26.5 SDK. I now have a complete picture. Let me provide the plan.

## Key Discovery: Most of the work is already done

Before the migration steps, the single most important finding: **the requested architecture is ~80% already implemented in this codebase.** The prompt's "What I already know" section describes an older state of the app. The current `main` branch (commit `86766b8`) already has:

- `BPMainWindowController` (`Cakebrew/BPMainWindowController.{h,m}`) — an `NSWindowController` that programmatically builds an `NSSplitViewController` with a true sidebar split item via `+[NSSplitViewItem sidebarWithViewController:]`.
- It's fully wired: `BPHomebrewViewController.viewDidLoad` (line 148) calls `[self.mainWindowController setUpViews]`, and the XIB has the `mainWindowController` outlet connected (`MainMenu.xib` line 749, object `Nan-E3-hfy`).
- `BPWindow.sharedInit` (`BPWindow.m` lines 31-40) already adds `NSWindowStyleMaskFullSizeContentView`.
- `BPToolbar` already inserts `NSToolbarSidebarTrackingSeparatorItemIdentifier` into its default item set (`BPToolbar.m` lines 185-193).

So objectives 1 (split view controller w/ sidebar item) and 3 (tracking separator) are effectively **already in place**. The real gaps are in objective 2 (unified toolbar style + transparent titlebar are *not* set anywhere) and in verifying/cleaning up the existing programmatic approach so the Tahoe glass look actually renders. Below is the precise current wiring, the recommended approach, and a file-by-file change list focused on the genuine gaps.

---

## 1. Current wiring (verified)

**App launch / window instantiation:**
- `main.m` → standard `NSApplicationMain`. `MainMenu.xib` is the main nib (File's Owner `-2` = `NSApplication`, delegate → `494` = `BPAppDelegate`).
- The window is object `371`, `customClass="BPWindow"`, style mask `titled|closable|miniaturizable|resizable` (no `fullSizeContentView` flag in the XIB — it's added at runtime in `BPWindow.sharedInit`). Its `contentView` is plain `NSView` id `372`.
- `BPAppDelegate.window` outlet → `371` (line 734). There is **no programmatic window controller showing the window** — the XIB owns and auto-displays it ("Visible at Launch" is the default for a XIB main window). `BPAppDelegate` only references the window for reopen/sheet purposes.

**How the view controller and split view attach (the important part):**
- `BPHomebrewViewController` is object `547`, a `viewController` in the same XIB with `nibName="MainMenu"`. Its `view` outlet → `372` (which is *also* the window's contentView). So the controller's `view` IS the window content view.
- `BPMainWindowController` is object `Nan-E3-hfy`. Its outlets: `window`→`371`, `sidebarView`→`bme-rl-6Ta` (the sidebar `NSScrollView`/outline), `windowContentView`→`du9-Lg-Fwn` (the content `customView` holding the tabView + footer stackView). Note: it is **not** set as the window's `windowController` and its `windowContentView` is a free-floating top-level object in the XIB, not initially in the view hierarchy.
- At runtime, `BPHomebrewViewController.viewDidLoad` calls `[self.mainWindowController setUpViews]`, which: creates `NSSplitViewController`, wraps `sidebarView` in a `+sidebarWithViewController:` item and `windowContentView` in a plain content item, then adds the split controller's `view` as a subview of the window's contentView (372) pinned with 4 constraints. So the live hierarchy is: `window(371).contentView(372)` → `splitViewController.view` → [sidebar item (bme-rl-6Ta), content item (du9-Lg-Fwn)].
- The old `splitView hkt-Ff-Ha2` is NOT the sidebar/content split. It is a *separate inner* vertical split (`formulaeSplitView` outlet) inside the content area holding the formulae table (`i6w-ej-a1P`) above the selected-formula box (`Nrf-M9-yac`). It is reparented into the Formulae tab at runtime (`viewDidLoad` lines 157-161). This is unrelated to the sidebar conversion and should be left alone.
- Toolbar: created programmatically in `BPHomebrewViewController.addToolbar` (lines 206-216): `[[BPToolbar alloc] initWithIdentifier:]`, set as `window.toolbar`, display mode IconOnly on macOS 11+.

**Sidebar selection contract:** `BPSideBarController` drives a real `NSOutlineView` (id `9f4-xo-e1c`, `selectionHighlightStyle="sourceList"`). The `FormulaeSideBarItem` enum (0–8, in `BPSideBarController.h`) maps directly to flat outline rows (2 group rows + 7 selectable rows). All selection logic in `BPHomebrewViewController` uses `self.sidebarController.sidebar selectedRow` / `selectRowIndexes:`. This outline view is the `sidebarView`'s document view and is moved wholesale into the sidebar split item — the flat-row indices are unaffected by the split-item wrapping.

---

## 2. Recommended migration approach

**Recommendation: keep the existing programmatic `NSSplitViewController` approach in `BPMainWindowController`; do NOT attempt to re-model this in the XIB.** Rationale:

- This is a single-XIB AppKit app where the window, its content view, and `BPHomebrewViewController.view` are the *same* object (372), and several top-level views are reparented at runtime. Converting the sidebar/content relationship to IB-native `NSSplitViewController` scenes would require splitting MainMenu.xib into multiple scenes/storyboard, re-homing every IBOutlet/IBAction/binding (there are dozens of bindings on the Formula menu alone), and re-establishing File's Owner relationships. That is high-risk for zero functional gain.
- The programmatic path already exists, compiles, and preserves every IBOutlet/IBAction and the flat-row-index sidebar contract because it only *re-parents* existing XIB views into split items — it never rebuilds them.
- The remaining gaps (unified toolbar style, transparent titlebar) are pure runtime property sets — trivially done in code, no XIB surgery.

So the migration is: **finish the runtime configuration that's missing, and make the glass actually show through.** The safest insertion point for window-level chrome is `BPMainWindowController.setUpViews` (it already holds the `window` outlet and runs once at load), or `BPWindow.sharedInit` for window-intrinsic flags.

---

## 3. Exact change list (file-by-file)

### A. `Cakebrew/BPMainWindowController.m` — add window chrome config (primary change)
In `setUpViews`, after the split controller view is installed (after line 49), configure the window for the unified/Tahoe look. Add a helper, e.g. `configureWindowChrome`, called at the end of `setUpViews`:
- `self.window.titlebarAppearsTransparent = YES;`
- `self.window.titleVisibility = NSWindowTitleVisible;` (keep "Cakebrew" title; unified toolbar shows it inline). Optionally `NSWindowTitleHidden` if you want a cleaner toolbar — decide visually.
- Toolbar style (the genuine objective-2 gap), guarded for the SDK:
  ```objc
  if (@available(macOS 11.0, *)) {
      self.window.toolbarStyle = NSWindowToolbarStyleUnified; // or ...UnifiedCompact
  }
  ```

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

## CRITICAL USER JOURNEYS IN CAKEBREW

### **APP STRUCTURE**

**Main Controllers:**
- `BPAppDelegate` — app lifecycle, Homebrew manager initialization
- `BPMainWindowController` — window layout with NSSplitViewController
- `BPHomebrewViewController` — main view controller; handles sidebar, formula table, tabs, and toolbar
- `BPSideBarController` — sidebar/outline view (hierarchical: Formulae category, Repositories category, Tools category)
- `BPToolbar` — dynamic toolbar with modes for install/uninstall/update/tap/untap
- `BPInstallationWindowController` — modal window for operation execution (install/uninstall/upgrade/tap/untap/cleanup)
- `BPUpdateViewController` — tab view for Homebrew update display
- `BPDoctorViewController` — tab view for Homebrew doctor display
- `BPFormulaPopoverViewController` — popover for formula info/dependents
- `BPFormulaOptionsWindowController` — modal for install options selection
- `BPSelectedFormulaViewController` — right panel with formula metadata

**XIB Files:**
- `MainMenu.xib` — menu bar structure (Formula, Tools menus + keyboard shortcuts)
- `BPInstallationWindow.xib` — operation progress window
- `BPUpdateView.xib`, `BPDoctorView.xib` — tabs
- `BPFormulaPopoverView.xib`, `BPFormulaOptionsWindow.xib`, `BPSelectedFormula.xib` — supporting views

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #1: BROWSE & VIEW INSTALLED FORMULAE**

**Goal:** User sees all installed packages and can examine individual package details.

**Entry Point:**  
- Sidebar: "Installed" item (FormulaeSideBarItemInstalled, line 170 BPSideBarController.m)

**Steps:**
1. App launches → `applicationDidFinishLaunching:` calls `reloadFromInterfaceRebuildingCache:NO` (BPAppDelegate.m:57)
2. BPHomebrewViewController loads, initializes BPFormulaeDataSource with `kBPListInstalled` mode
3. Sidebar delegates `sourceListSelectionDidChange:` → calls `configureTableForListing:kBPListInstalled` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:595)
4. Table columns configured: Name (40%), Version (55%) shown; Status/LatestVersion hidden (BPFormulaeTableView.m:61-65)
5. User clicks formula row → `formulaeTableView` selection updates; `updateInterfaceItems` configures toolbar to "Uninstall" mode (BPHomebrewViewController.m:330)
6. Selected formula details appear in right panel via `BPSelectedFormulaViewController` showing: description, path, version, dependencies, conflicts (BPSelectedFormulaViewController.h:25-29)

**Observable Results:**
- Sidebar "Installed" badge shows count (e.g., "42")
- Table lists installed formulae with current version
- Right panel shows metadata for selected formula
- Toolbar "Uninstall" button enabled

**Dependencies:**
- **Requires real Homebrew install** — `BPHomebrewInterface` directly calls `brew list` and `brew info` commands
- If Homebrew not detected: delegate callback `homebrewInterfaceShouldDisplayNoBrewMessage:YES` triggers disabled view (BPHomebrewInterface.h:47, BPHomebrewViewController.m:74)

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #2: SEARCH FOR A FORMULA**

**Goal:** User finds a package not yet installed by name.

**Entry Point:**  
- Toolbar: Search field (visible in all modes)  
- OR Menu > Formula > "Search for Formula" (Cmd+F, MainMenu.xib:232)

**Steps:**
1. User focuses search field via `beginFormulaSearch:` → `makeSearchFieldFirstResponder` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:849, BPToolbar.m:55)
2. User types search text (e.g., "node")
3. Toolbar delegate calls `performSearchWithString:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:837)
4. `BPHomebrewManager updateSearchWithName:` queries Homebrew in background
5. Search results update table via delegate callback `homebrewManager:didUpdateSearchResults:` (BPHomebrewManager.h:36)
6. Table switches to search result data source showing all matching formulae (installed, outdated, not installed)
7. User selects a result → right panel shows formula metadata including install status (BPSelectedFormulaViewController)

**Observable Results:**
- Search field shows typed text
- Table dynamically updates with matching formulae
- Right panel shows details + install button if not installed
- Toolbar switches to "Install" mode when non-installed formula selected

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew (`brew search`)
- Search is async; `BPLoadingView` may appear during search

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #3: INSTALL A FORMULA**

**Goal:** User installs a new package.

**Entry Points:**
- Toolbar: "Install" button (when non-installed formula selected)
- Menu > Formula > "Install Formula" (Return key, MainMenu.xib:78)
- Menu > Formula > "Install Formula with Options…" (Opt+Return, MainMenu.xib:101)

**Steps (Basic Install):**
1. User selects non-installed formula; toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeInstall` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:342)
2. User clicks "Install" button → `installFormula:` action (BPHomebrewViewController.m:661)
3. Confirmation alert appears: "Are you sure you want to install {formula}?" (line 669-674)
4. User clicks "Yes" → `BPInstallationWindowController runWithOperation:kBPWindowOperationInstall formulae:options:` opens modal window (line 679)
5. Installation window shows:
   - Title: "Installing Formula:"
   - Formula name(s)
   - Progress spinner
   - Auto-scrolling text view with brew command output
   - "OK" button (disabled during execution)
6. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew install {formula}` in background
7. Command output streams to window
8. When done, "OK" button enabled; user closes window

**Steps (Install with Options):**
1. User selects non-installed formula
2. User presses Opt+Return (or menu) → `installFormulaWithOptions:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:685)
3. `BPFormulaOptionsWindowController runFormula:withCompletionBlock:` shows modal listing formula build options (checkboxes)
4. User selects options, clicks "Install"
5. Completion block triggers installation window (same as above) with selected options passed

**Observable Results:**
- Modal window appears with live command output
- Formula moves to "Installed" sidebar after completion
- "Installed" badge count increments
- Installed list auto-refreshes

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew + formula downloadable
- May require network (downloading formula/dependencies)
- Some formulae require compilation (time-consuming)

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #4: UNINSTALL A FORMULA**

**Goal:** User removes an installed package.

**Entry Point:**
- Toolbar: "Uninstall" button (when installed formula selected)
- Menu > Formula > "Uninstall Formula" (Ctrl+U, MainMenu.xib:124)

**Steps:**
1. User selects installed formula → toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeUninstall` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:330)
2. User clicks "Uninstall" → `uninstallFormula:` action (BPHomebrewViewController.m:699)
3. Confirmation alert: "Are you sure you want to uninstall {formula}?"
4. User clicks "Yes" → opens `BPInstallationWindowController` with `kBPWindowOperationUninstall`
5. Installation window executes `brew uninstall {formula}` with output streaming
6. Formula removed from installed list upon completion

**Observable Results:**
- Modal progress window
- Formula disappears from "Installed" list
- Badge count decrements
- Toolbar switches to "Install" mode for that formula

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew + formula currently installed
- May fail if formula is depended on by other installed packages (user sees error in window)

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #5: UPGRADE/UPDATE AN OUTDATED FORMULA**

**Goal:** User updates a single outdated package or bulk-updates all outdated packages.

**Entry Points:**
- Sidebar: "Outdated" item → select formula → Toolbar "Update" button  
- Toolbar/Menu: "Upgrade Selected Formulae" (Cmd+U, MainMenu.xib:219)
- Menu: "Upgrade All Formulae" (Opt+Cmd+U, MainMenu.xib:225)

**Steps (Single Upgrade):**
1. User clicks "Outdated" sidebar item (FormulaeSideBarItemOutdated, line 175 BPSideBarController.m)
2. Table shows only outdated formulae (Name + current/latest versions)
3. User selects one → toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeUpdateSingle` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:335)
4. User clicks toolbar "Update" or presses Cmd+R → `upgradeSelectedFormulae:` (line 723)
5. Installation window with `kBPWindowOperationUpgrade` executes `brew upgrade {formula}`
6. Upon completion, formula updates in "Outdated" list (or disappears if now up-to-date)

**Steps (Bulk Upgrade):**
1. User in "Outdated" view
2. User selects multiple formulae (Shift/Cmd+click enabled, BPFormulaeTableView.m:57 sets `allowsMultipleSelection:NO` for most views, but batch operations exist)
3. Toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeUpdateMany` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:322) if 1+ selected
4. User clicks "Update" or presses Opt+Cmd+U → `upgradeAllOutdatedFormulae:` (line 749)
5. Installation window executes `brew upgrade` on all selected/outdated
6. All outdated formulae updated in single operation

**Observable Results:**
- "Outdated" badge shows count of outdated
- After upgrade, formula version updates in list
- Outdated list shrinks as formulae update
- Toolbar button labels change based on selection count

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew
- Formula must have available newer version
- May require network for downloads

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #6: MANAGE REPOSITORIES (TAP/UNTAP)**

**Goal:** User adds/removes third-party formula repositories.

**Entry Points:**
- Sidebar: "Repositories" item (FormulaeSideBarItemRepositories, line 190 BPSideBarController.m)
- Toolbar: "Tap" / "Untap" buttons (context-dependent)

**Steps (Add Repository/Tap):**
1. User clicks "Repositories" sidebar item → table shows list of tapped repos (line 610-611)
2. Table is empty or shows existing taps
3. Toolbar shows "Tap" button (BPToolbarModeTap, line 307)
4. User clicks "Tap" or uses toolbar → `tapRepository:` action (line 768)
5. Alert appears: "Enter repository name (e.g., user/repo)"
6. User enters repo name (e.g., "homebrew/cask"), clicks "OK"
7. Installation window opens with `kBPWindowOperationTap`, executes `brew tap {repo}`
8. Upon completion, new repo appears in repositories list

**Steps (Remove Repository/Untap):**
1. User clicks "Repositories" sidebar item
2. User selects a tapped repository from list
3. Toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeUntap` (line 311)
4. User clicks "Untap" → `untapRepository:` action (line 797)
5. Confirmation alert: "Are you sure you want to untap {repo}?"
6. Installation window executes `brew untap {repo}`
7. Repo removed from list upon completion

**Observable Results:**
- "Repositories" badge shows count of tapped repos
- List updates with new/removed repos
- Repository-specific formulae become available/unavailable in search

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew
- Repo name must be valid and publicly available (for tap)

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #7: RUN HOMEBREW DOCTOR**

**Goal:** User diagnoses Homebrew installation issues.

**Entry Point:**
- Sidebar: "Doctor" item (FormulaeSideBarItemDoctor, line 199 BPSideBarController.m)

**Steps:**
1. User clicks "Doctor" sidebar → tab view switches to Doctor tab (line 614-615)
2. BPDoctorViewController view shows:
   - Title: "Homebrew Doctor"
   - Progress spinner
   - Auto-scrolling text view (empty initially)
   - "Clear Log" button (Cmd+K)
   - "Run Doctor" button
3. User clicks "Run Doctor" → `runStopDoctor:` (BPDoctorViewController.m:13)
4. Button text changes to "Stop"; progress spinner animates
5. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew doctor` in background
6. Output streams into text view in real-time
7. Upon completion, button re-enables (text → "Run Doctor")
8. User can review output or click "Run Doctor" again

**Observable Results:**
- Doctor tab active
- Real-time command output visible
- Button state changes (disabled → enabled after completion)
- Badge on sidebar item shows warning count (if issues found)

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew
- Doctor command only outputs warnings/advice; doesn't modify system

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #8: UPDATE HOMEBREW ITSELF**

**Goal:** User updates Homebrew package manager to latest version.

**Entry Points:**
- Sidebar: "Update" item (FormulaeSideBarItemUpdate, line 205 BPSideBarController.m)
- Toolbar: "Update Homebrew" button (when Update tab visible)
- Menu > Formula > (implicit via update check)

**Steps:**
1. User clicks "Update" sidebar → tab view switches to Update tab (line 618-619)
2. BPUpdateViewController view shows:
   - Title: "Homebrew Updater"
   - Progress spinner
   - Auto-scrolling text view (empty initially)
   - "Clear Log" button (Cmd+K)
   - "Update Homebrew" button
3. User clicks "Update Homebrew" → `runStopUpdate:` (BPUpdateViewController.m:13)
4. Executes `brew update` in background
5. Real-time output streams to text view
6. Upon completion, button re-enables
7. User can review results (new packages available, etc.)

**Observable Results:**
- Update tab active
- Live command output showing Homebrew components updated
- All formulae lists refresh after update (may show newly available versions)
- "Outdated" badge may change if new versions now available

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew
- Requires network to fetch latest Homebrew repository

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #9: IMPORT/EXPORT BREWFILE**

**Goal:** User backs up or restores Homebrew installation configuration.

**Entry Points:**
- Menu > Tools > "Export Brew Installation…" (MainMenu.xib:253)
- Menu > Tools > "Import Brew Installation…" (MainMenu.xib:260)

**Steps (Export):**
1. User clicks Menu > Tools > "Export Brew Installation…" → `runHomebrewExport:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:861)
2. File save dialog appears (NSSavePanel, delegate: BPHomebrewViewController)
3. User selects location, names file (e.g., "Brewfile"), clicks "Save"
4. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew bundle dump --file={path}` (requires homebrew-bundle tap)
5. File generated in selected location
6. Dialog may alert if homebrew-bundle not installed; offers to install it

**Steps (Import):**
1. User clicks Menu > Tools > "Import Brew Installation…" → `runHomebrewImport:` (line 881)
2. File open dialog appears (NSOpenPanel, delegate: BPHomebrewViewController)
3. User selects Brewfile, clicks "Open"
4. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew bundle install --file={path}`
5. Homebrew installs all formulae listed in Brewfile
6. Installation window shows progress output

**Observable Results:**
- For export: Brewfile created at user's chosen location
- For import: all formulae in Brewfile installed; sidebar badges update

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew + homebrew-bundle tap
- If homebrew-bundle not installed, user sees tap installation prompt

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #10: CLEANUP UNUSED DEPENDENCIES**

**Goal:** User removes unused/orphaned packages.

**Entry Point:**
- Menu > Tools > "Brew Cleanup…" (MainMenu.xib:245)

**Steps:**
1. User clicks Menu > Tools > "Brew Cleanup…" → `runHomebrewCleanup:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:854)
2. Installation window opens with `kBPWindowOperationCleanup`
3. Title: "Cleanup"
4. No formula names shown (generic cleanup)
5. Progress spinner + auto-scrolling text view
6. Executes `brew cleanup` in background
7. Output shows removed packages and freed space
8. User closes window when done

**Observable Results:**
- Modal window with live output
- Disk space may be freed
- Package lists may refresh (removed formulae disappear)

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #11: VIEW FORMULA DETAILS & DEPENDENCIES**

**Goal:** User inspects detailed info about a formula and its dependents.

**Entry Points:**
- Right-click formula → "More Information" (context menu from BPFormulaeTableView)
- Toolbar: "More Information" button (enabled for single formula selection, not for tap/multi-select)
- Menu > Formula > "More Information" (Cmd+I, MainMenu.xib:164)
- Menu > Formula > "List Installed Dependents" (MainMenu.xib:175)
- Menu > Formula > "List All Dependents" (Opt+click, MainMenu.xib:186)

**Steps:**
1. User selects a formula in table
2. User clicks "More Information" or presses Cmd+I → `showFormulaInfo:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:640)
3. BPFormulaPopoverViewController launches as popover near table
4. Popover shows:
   - Formula title
   - Progress spinner (loading)
   - Text view with formula info (description, homepage, etc.)
5. For dependents, user selects alt-variant:
   - "List Installed Dependents" → shows only installed dependents (line 645, type = kBPFormulaInfoTypeInstalledDependents)
   - "List All Dependents" (Opt+variant) → shows all dependents incl. not installed (type = kBPFormulaInfoTypeAllDependents)
6. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew info {formula}` or `brew uses {formula}` asynchronously
7. Popover text updates with results
8. User closes popover by clicking elsewhere

**Observable Results:**
- Popover appears anchored to formula row
- Live info loads progressively
- Dependencies list visible for formula

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew (`brew info`, `brew uses`)
- Async loading (progress indicator)

---

### **ACCESSIBILITY & UI TESTABILITY ASSESSMENT**

#### **Accessibility Labels Currently Set:**

| Element | File:Line | Label |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Sidebar (OutlineView) | BPSideBarController.m:289 | "Sidebar_VoiceOver_Tools" (localized) |
| Formula Table | BPHomebrewViewController.m:154 | "Formulae" |
| Formula Options Table | BPFormulaOptionsWindowController.m | "Formula_Options_VoiceOver" |
| Formula Options Description Field | BPFormulaOptionsWindowController.m | "Formula_Options_VoiceOver_Description" |
| Individual Option Cells | BPFormulaOptionsWindowController.m | Dynamic label from option description |
| Sidebar Icons | BPSideBarController.m:216-277 | `accessibilityDescription` on SF Symbols (Installed, Outdated, All, Leaves, Repos, Doctor, Update) |

#### **Missing Accessibility Identifiers:**

**Critical gaps for XCUITest selectors:**

| UI Element | Location | Issue |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| Toolbar buttons | BPToolbar.m | No `setAccessibilityIdentifier` — dynamically configured by mode; use label lookup only |
| Search field | BPToolbar.m | No identifier; can find via label "Search" or by index |
| Formula table rows | BPFormulaeTableView.m | No identifiers on cells; must use row index or formula name |
| Sidebar items | BPSideBarController.m (line 348) | Header/Item cells created via `makeViewWithIdentifier:@"HeaderCell"/@"MainCell"` but no accessibility ID on content |
| Installation window elements | BPInstallationWindow.xib | Window outlets set (formulaNameLabel, recordTextView, progressIndicator, okButton) but no accessibility IDs in XIB |
| Update/Doctor buttons | BPUpdateView.xib, BPDoctorView.xib | Buttons have `id` in XIB but no `setAccessibilityIdentifier` calls in code |
| Alert dialogs | BPHomebrewViewController.m (lines 669, 707, 772, 807) | Standard NSAlert — no custom identifiers; must match by button title |
| Menu items | MainMenu.xib | Bound to actions; no accessibility identifiers |
| Installation progress window | BPInstallationWindowController.m | No accessibility ID on window itself |

#### **XCUITest Implications:**

**RELIABLE (use these):**
- `XCUIApplication().windows["Installation"]` — window title is "Installing Formula:", "Uninstalling Formula:", etc. (BPInstallationWindow.xib)
- Sidebar items via `staticTexts["Installed"]`, `staticTexts["Outdated"]`, etc. (sidebar uses outline view with text cells)
- Formula table via row/column queries
- Menu items via `menuItems["Install Formula"]` pattern

**FRAGILE (avoid or add workarounds):**
- Toolbar buttons — must query by label (which changes based on context/mode)
- Search field — find by label or nth-child positioning
- Alert buttons — must match by localized button title strings
- Installation window controls — no IDs; must use outlets (internal only) or find via type + parent window

#### **Recommended Test Fixes:**

1. **Add accessibility identifiers to XIB files:**
   ```
   Installation window: addAccessibilityIdentifier: @"InstallationProgressWindow"
   Installation OK button: addAccessibilityIdentifier: @"InstallationOKButton"
   Update "Update Homebrew" button: addAccessibilityIdentifier: @"UpdateHomebrewButton"
   Doctor "Run Doctor" button: addAccessibilityIdentifier: @"RunDoctorButton"
   Search field: addAccessibilityIdentifier: @"ToolbarSearchField"
   ```

2. **Add accessibility IDs to toolbar buttons in code** (BPToolbar.m `reconfigureItem:` methods):
   ```
   [toolbarItem setAccessibilityIdentifier:@"ToolbarInstallButton"]
   [toolbarItem setAccessibilityIdentifier:@"ToolbarUninstallButton"]
   etc.
   ```

3. **Sidebar items** — already have text labels; query by `staticTexts[label]` is reliable.

4. **Formula table** — use row/column indexing or match formula name in Name column.

---

### **HOMEBREW DEPENDENCY: CRITICAL FOR ALL JOURNEYS**

**All 11 journeys require a real, working Homebrew installation.** Tests cannot run without:
- `brew` command in PATH
- Homebrew configured and able to execute operations
- Network access (for search, install, update, tap operations)
- Sufficient disk space for installs

**Test Strategy Recommendation:**
- Use **mock Homebrew interface** (BPHomebrewInterface.h could be wrapped) for unit tests
- For **integration/UI tests**: either
  - Provision a test VM with Homebrew pre-installed
  - Use **stubbed Homebrew commands** that return fixed data
  - Accept that UI tests require full Homebrew environment

**No Homebrew Scenario:**
- App shows `BPDisabledView` (dark overlay + message "Homebrew not installed")
- Sidebar clickable but table empty
- Operations disabled
- Relevant for testing error handling, but not for critical journeys

---

### **SUMMARY TABLE: 11 CRITICAL USER JOURNEYS**

| # | Journey | Entry Point | Key Files | Real Homebrew? | Accessibility |
|---|---------|------------|-----------|----------------|---|
| 1 | Browse Installed | Sidebar "Installed" | BPHomebrewViewController.m:594-595 | ✓ Required | ✓ Sidebar label set |
| 2 | Search Formula | Toolbar/Menu search | BPHomebrewViewController.m:849 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Search field no ID |
| 3 | Install | Toolbar/Menu | BPHomebrewViewController.m:661 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Alert no ID, button no ID |
| 4 | Uninstall | Toolbar/Menu | BPHomebrewViewController.m:699 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Alert no ID, button no ID |
| 5 | Upgrade | Outdated sidebar | BPHomebrewViewController.m:723, 749 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Toolbar button no ID |
| 6 | Tap/Untap Repos | Sidebar "Repositories" | BPHomebrewViewController.m:768, 797 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Alert/input no ID, toolbar no ID |
| 7 | Run Doctor | Sidebar "Doctor" | BPDoctorViewController.m:13 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Button no ID in XIB |
| 8 | Update Homebrew | Sidebar "Update" | BPUpdateViewController.m:13 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Button no ID in XIB |
| 9 | Import/Export | Menu > Tools | BPHomebrewViewController.m:861, 881 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Dialogs auto-generated (NSOpenPanel/NSSavePanel) |
| 10 | Cleanup | Menu > Tools | BPHomebrewViewController.m:854 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Window no ID |
| 11 | View Details/Deps | Toolbar/Menu "More Info" | BPHomebrewViewController.m:640, 645 | ✓ Required | ⚠ Popover no accessibility setup |

---

### **KEY FILE REFERENCES**

**Controllers:**
- `/Cakebrew/Controllers/BPHomebrewViewController.{h,m}` — main view logic, 16 IBActions
- `/Cakebrew/Controllers/BPSideBarController.{h,m}` — sidebar model + delegate

**View/UI:**

content.text:
## CRITICAL USER JOURNEYS IN CAKEBREW

### **APP STRUCTURE**

**Main Controllers:**
- `BPAppDelegate` — app lifecycle, Homebrew manager initialization
- `BPMainWindowController` — window layout with NSSplitViewController
- `BPHomebrewViewController` — main view controller; handles sidebar, formula table, tabs, and toolbar
- `BPSideBarController` — sidebar/outline view (hierarchical: Formulae category, Repositories category, Tools category)
- `BPToolbar` — dynamic toolbar with modes for install/uninstall/update/tap/untap
- `BPInstallationWindowController` — modal window for operation execution (install/uninstall/upgrade/tap/untap/cleanup)
- `BPUpdateViewController` — tab view for Homebrew update display
- `BPDoctorViewController` — tab view for Homebrew doctor display
- `BPFormulaPopoverViewController` — popover for formula info/dependents
- `BPFormulaOptionsWindowController` — modal for install options selection
- `BPSelectedFormulaViewController` — right panel with formula metadata

**XIB Files:**
- `MainMenu.xib` — menu bar structure (Formula, Tools menus + keyboard shortcuts)
- `BPInstallationWindow.xib` — operation progress window
- `BPUpdateView.xib`, `BPDoctorView.xib` — tabs
- `BPFormulaPopoverView.xib`, `BPFormulaOptionsWindow.xib`, `BPSelectedFormula.xib` — supporting views

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #1: BROWSE & VIEW INSTALLED FORMULAE**

**Goal:** User sees all installed packages and can examine individual package details.

**Entry Point:**  
- Sidebar: "Installed" item (FormulaeSideBarItemInstalled, line 170 BPSideBarController.m)

**Steps:**
1. App launches → `applicationDidFinishLaunching:` calls `reloadFromInterfaceRebuildingCache:NO` (BPAppDelegate.m:57)
2. BPHomebrewViewController loads, initializes BPFormulaeDataSource with `kBPListInstalled` mode
3. Sidebar delegates `sourceListSelectionDidChange:` → calls `configureTableForListing:kBPListInstalled` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:595)
4. Table columns configured: Name (40%), Version (55%) shown; Status/LatestVersion hidden (BPFormulaeTableView.m:61-65)
5. User clicks formula row → `formulaeTableView` selection updates; `updateInterfaceItems` configures toolbar to "Uninstall" mode (BPHomebrewViewController.m:330)
6. Selected formula details appear in right panel via `BPSelectedFormulaViewController` showing: description, path, version, dependencies, conflicts (BPSelectedFormulaViewController.h:25-29)

**Observable Results:**
- Sidebar "Installed" badge shows count (e.g., "42")
- Table lists installed formulae with current version
- Right panel shows metadata for selected formula
- Toolbar "Uninstall" button enabled

**Dependencies:**
- **Requires real Homebrew install** — `BPHomebrewInterface` directly calls `brew list` and `brew info` commands
- If Homebrew not detected: delegate callback `homebrewInterfaceShouldDisplayNoBrewMessage:YES` triggers disabled view (BPHomebrewInterface.h:47, BPHomebrewViewController.m:74)

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #2: SEARCH FOR A FORMULA**

**Goal:** User finds a package not yet installed by name.

**Entry Point:**  
- Toolbar: Search field (visible in all modes)  
- OR Menu > Formula > "Search for Formula" (Cmd+F, MainMenu.xib:232)

**Steps:**
1. User focuses search field via `beginFormulaSearch:` → `makeSearchFieldFirstResponder` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:849, BPToolbar.m:55)
2. User types search text (e.g., "node")
3. Toolbar delegate calls `performSearchWithString:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:837)
4. `BPHomebrewManager updateSearchWithName:` queries Homebrew in background
5. Search results update table via delegate callback `homebrewManager:didUpdateSearchResults:` (BPHomebrewManager.h:36)
6. Table switches to search result data source showing all matching formulae (installed, outdated, not installed)
7. User selects a result → right panel shows formula metadata including install status (BPSelectedFormulaViewController)

**Observable Results:**
- Search field shows typed text
- Table dynamically updates with matching formulae
- Right panel shows details + install button if not installed
- Toolbar switches to "Install" mode when non-installed formula selected

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew (`brew search`)
- Search is async; `BPLoadingView` may appear during search

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #3: INSTALL A FORMULA**

**Goal:** User installs a new package.

**Entry Points:**
- Toolbar: "Install" button (when non-installed formula selected)
- Menu > Formula > "Install Formula" (Return key, MainMenu.xib:78)
- Menu > Formula > "Install Formula with Options…" (Opt+Return, MainMenu.xib:101)

**Steps (Basic Install):**
1. User selects non-installed formula; toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeInstall` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:342)
2. User clicks "Install" button → `installFormula:` action (BPHomebrewViewController.m:661)
3. Confirmation alert appears: "Are you sure you want to install {formula}?" (line 669-674)
4. User clicks "Yes" → `BPInstallationWindowController runWithOperation:kBPWindowOperationInstall formulae:options:` opens modal window (line 679)
5. Installation window shows:
   - Title: "Installing Formula:"
   - Formula name(s)
   - Progress spinner
   - Auto-scrolling text view with brew command output
   - "OK" button (disabled during execution)
6. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew install {formula}` in background
7. Command output streams to window
8. When done, "OK" button enabled; user closes window

**Steps (Install with Options):**
1. User selects non-installed formula
2. User presses Opt+Return (or menu) → `installFormulaWithOptions:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:685)
3. `BPFormulaOptionsWindowController runFormula:withCompletionBlock:` shows modal listing formula build options (checkboxes)
4. User selects options, clicks "Install"
5. Completion block triggers installation window (same as above) with selected options passed

**Observable Results:**
- Modal window appears with live command output
- Formula moves to "Installed" sidebar after completion
- "Installed" badge count increments
- Installed list auto-refreshes

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew + formula downloadable
- May require network (downloading formula/dependencies)
- Some formulae require compilation (time-consuming)

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #4: UNINSTALL A FORMULA**

**Goal:** User removes an installed package.

**Entry Point:**
- Toolbar: "Uninstall" button (when installed formula selected)
- Menu > Formula > "Uninstall Formula" (Ctrl+U, MainMenu.xib:124)

**Steps:**
1. User selects installed formula → toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeUninstall` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:330)
2. User clicks "Uninstall" → `uninstallFormula:` action (BPHomebrewViewController.m:699)
3. Confirmation alert: "Are you sure you want to uninstall {formula}?"
4. User clicks "Yes" → opens `BPInstallationWindowController` with `kBPWindowOperationUninstall`
5. Installation window executes `brew uninstall {formula}` with output streaming
6. Formula removed from installed list upon completion

**Observable Results:**
- Modal progress window
- Formula disappears from "Installed" list
- Badge count decrements
- Toolbar switches to "Install" mode for that formula

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew + formula currently installed
- May fail if formula is depended on by other installed packages (user sees error in window)

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #5: UPGRADE/UPDATE AN OUTDATED FORMULA**

**Goal:** User updates a single outdated package or bulk-updates all outdated packages.

**Entry Points:**
- Sidebar: "Outdated" item → select formula → Toolbar "Update" button  
- Toolbar/Menu: "Upgrade Selected Formulae" (Cmd+U, MainMenu.xib:219)
- Menu: "Upgrade All Formulae" (Opt+Cmd+U, MainMenu.xib:225)

**Steps (Single Upgrade):**
1. User clicks "Outdated" sidebar item (FormulaeSideBarItemOutdated, line 175 BPSideBarController.m)
2. Table shows only outdated formulae (Name + current/latest versions)
3. User selects one → toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeUpdateSingle` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:335)
4. User clicks toolbar "Update" or presses Cmd+R → `upgradeSelectedFormulae:` (line 723)
5. Installation window with `kBPWindowOperationUpgrade` executes `brew upgrade {formula}`
6. Upon completion, formula updates in "Outdated" list (or disappears if now up-to-date)

**Steps (Bulk Upgrade):**
1. User in "Outdated" view
2. User selects multiple formulae (Shift/Cmd+click enabled, BPFormulaeTableView.m:57 sets `allowsMultipleSelection:NO` for most views, but batch operations exist)
3. Toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeUpdateMany` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:322) if 1+ selected
4. User clicks "Update" or presses Opt+Cmd+U → `upgradeAllOutdatedFormulae:` (line 749)
5. Installation window executes `brew upgrade` on all selected/outdated
6. All outdated formulae updated in single operation

**Observable Results:**
- "Outdated" badge shows count of outdated
- After upgrade, formula version updates in list
- Outdated list shrinks as formulae update
- Toolbar button labels change based on selection count

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew
- Formula must have available newer version
- May require network for downloads

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #6: MANAGE REPOSITORIES (TAP/UNTAP)**

**Goal:** User adds/removes third-party formula repositories.

**Entry Points:**
- Sidebar: "Repositories" item (FormulaeSideBarItemRepositories, line 190 BPSideBarController.m)
- Toolbar: "Tap" / "Untap" buttons (context-dependent)

**Steps (Add Repository/Tap):**
1. User clicks "Repositories" sidebar item → table shows list of tapped repos (line 610-611)
2. Table is empty or shows existing taps
3. Toolbar shows "Tap" button (BPToolbarModeTap, line 307)
4. User clicks "Tap" or uses toolbar → `tapRepository:` action (line 768)
5. Alert appears: "Enter repository name (e.g., user/repo)"
6. User enters repo name (e.g., "homebrew/cask"), clicks "OK"
7. Installation window opens with `kBPWindowOperationTap`, executes `brew tap {repo}`
8. Upon completion, new repo appears in repositories list

**Steps (Remove Repository/Untap):**
1. User clicks "Repositories" sidebar item
2. User selects a tapped repository from list
3. Toolbar configures to `BPToolbarModeUntap` (line 311)
4. User clicks "Untap" → `untapRepository:` action (line 797)
5. Confirmation alert: "Are you sure you want to untap {repo}?"
6. Installation window executes `brew untap {repo}`
7. Repo removed from list upon completion

**Observable Results:**
- "Repositories" badge shows count of tapped repos
- List updates with new/removed repos
- Repository-specific formulae become available/unavailable in search

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew
- Repo name must be valid and publicly available (for tap)

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #7: RUN HOMEBREW DOCTOR**

**Goal:** User diagnoses Homebrew installation issues.

**Entry Point:**
- Sidebar: "Doctor" item (FormulaeSideBarItemDoctor, line 199 BPSideBarController.m)

**Steps:**
1. User clicks "Doctor" sidebar → tab view switches to Doctor tab (line 614-615)
2. BPDoctorViewController view shows:
   - Title: "Homebrew Doctor"
   - Progress spinner
   - Auto-scrolling text view (empty initially)
   - "Clear Log" button (Cmd+K)
   - "Run Doctor" button
3. User clicks "Run Doctor" → `runStopDoctor:` (BPDoctorViewController.m:13)
4. Button text changes to "Stop"; progress spinner animates
5. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew doctor` in background
6. Output streams into text view in real-time
7. Upon completion, button re-enables (text → "Run Doctor")
8. User can review output or click "Run Doctor" again

**Observable Results:**
- Doctor tab active
- Real-time command output visible
- Button state changes (disabled → enabled after completion)
- Badge on sidebar item shows warning count (if issues found)

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew
- Doctor command only outputs warnings/advice; doesn't modify system

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #8: UPDATE HOMEBREW ITSELF**

**Goal:** User updates Homebrew package manager to latest version.

**Entry Points:**
- Sidebar: "Update" item (FormulaeSideBarItemUpdate, line 205 BPSideBarController.m)
- Toolbar: "Update Homebrew" button (when Update tab visible)
- Menu > Formula > (implicit via update check)

**Steps:**
1. User clicks "Update" sidebar → tab view switches to Update tab (line 618-619)
2. BPUpdateViewController view shows:
   - Title: "Homebrew Updater"
   - Progress spinner
   - Auto-scrolling text view (empty initially)
   - "Clear Log" button (Cmd+K)
   - "Update Homebrew" button
3. User clicks "Update Homebrew" → `runStopUpdate:` (BPUpdateViewController.m:13)
4. Executes `brew update` in background
5. Real-time output streams to text view
6. Upon completion, button re-enables
7. User can review results (new packages available, etc.)

**Observable Results:**
- Update tab active
- Live command output showing Homebrew components updated
- All formulae lists refresh after update (may show newly available versions)
- "Outdated" badge may change if new versions now available

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew
- Requires network to fetch latest Homebrew repository

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #9: IMPORT/EXPORT BREWFILE**

**Goal:** User backs up or restores Homebrew installation configuration.

**Entry Points:**
- Menu > Tools > "Export Brew Installation…" (MainMenu.xib:253)
- Menu > Tools > "Import Brew Installation…" (MainMenu.xib:260)

**Steps (Export):**
1. User clicks Menu > Tools > "Export Brew Installation…" → `runHomebrewExport:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:861)
2. File save dialog appears (NSSavePanel, delegate: BPHomebrewViewController)
3. User selects location, names file (e.g., "Brewfile"), clicks "Save"
4. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew bundle dump --file={path}` (requires homebrew-bundle tap)
5. File generated in selected location
6. Dialog may alert if homebrew-bundle not installed; offers to install it

**Steps (Import):**
1. User clicks Menu > Tools > "Import Brew Installation…" → `runHomebrewImport:` (line 881)
2. File open dialog appears (NSOpenPanel, delegate: BPHomebrewViewController)
3. User selects Brewfile, clicks "Open"
4. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew bundle install --file={path}`
5. Homebrew installs all formulae listed in Brewfile
6. Installation window shows progress output

**Observable Results:**
- For export: Brewfile created at user's chosen location
- For import: all formulae in Brewfile installed; sidebar badges update

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew + homebrew-bundle tap
- If homebrew-bundle not installed, user sees tap installation prompt

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #10: CLEANUP UNUSED DEPENDENCIES**

**Goal:** User removes unused/orphaned packages.

**Entry Point:**
- Menu > Tools > "Brew Cleanup…" (MainMenu.xib:245)

**Steps:**
1. User clicks Menu > Tools > "Brew Cleanup…" → `runHomebrewCleanup:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:854)
2. Installation window opens with `kBPWindowOperationCleanup`
3. Title: "Cleanup"
4. No formula names shown (generic cleanup)
5. Progress spinner + auto-scrolling text view
6. Executes `brew cleanup` in background
7. Output shows removed packages and freed space
8. User closes window when done

**Observable Results:**
- Modal window with live output
- Disk space may be freed
- Package lists may refresh (removed formulae disappear)

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew

---

### **CRITICAL JOURNEY #11: VIEW FORMULA DETAILS & DEPENDENCIES**

**Goal:** User inspects detailed info about a formula and its dependents.

**Entry Points:**
- Right-click formula → "More Information" (context menu from BPFormulaeTableView)
- Toolbar: "More Information" button (enabled for single formula selection, not for tap/multi-select)
- Menu > Formula > "More Information" (Cmd+I, MainMenu.xib:164)
- Menu > Formula > "List Installed Dependents" (MainMenu.xib:175)
- Menu > Formula > "List All Dependents" (Opt+click, MainMenu.xib:186)

**Steps:**
1. User selects a formula in table
2. User clicks "More Information" or presses Cmd+I → `showFormulaInfo:` (BPHomebrewViewController.m:640)
3. BPFormulaPopoverViewController launches as popover near table
4. Popover shows:
   - Formula title
   - Progress spinner (loading)
   - Text view with formula info (description, homepage, etc.)
5. For dependents, user selects alt-variant:
   - "List Installed Dependents" → shows only installed dependents (line 645, type = kBPFormulaInfoTypeInstalledDependents)
   - "List All Dependents" (Opt+variant) → shows all dependents incl. not installed (type = kBPFormulaInfoTypeAllDependents)
6. BPHomebrewInterface executes `brew info {formula}` or `brew uses {formula}` asynchronously
7. Popover text updates with results
8. User closes popover by clicking elsewhere

**Observable Results:**
- Popover appears anchored to formula row
- Live info loads progressively
- Dependencies list visible for formula

**Dependencies:**
- Requires real Homebrew (`brew info`, `brew uses`)
- Async loading (progress indicator)

### **ACCESSIBILITY & UI TESTABILITY ASSESSMENT**

#### **Accessibility Labels Currently Set:**

| Element | File:Line | Label |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Sidebar (OutlineView) | BPSideBarController.m:289 | "Sidebar_VoiceOver_Tools" (localized) |
| Formula Table | BPHomebrewViewController.m:154 | "Formulae" |
