content.text:
I'll skip a speculative diagram and give you the actionable plan directly — you're working in a terminal and these are TDD-ready specs you can start from. (Happy to spin this into a shareable one-page artifact if you want it for collaborators.)

# Cakebrew feature plan

The recon confirmed the codebase makes list-based sections cheap to add — the pattern is always: **`BPListMode` case → a `BPHomebrewInterfaceListCall` subclass (args + line parser) → a `BPHomebrewManager` property → a sidebar item → mock fixture**. Every feature below reuses that groove, and each has a **pure parser function** that's the natural TDD seam (test-first, no real Homebrew needed).

---

## M1 — Quick wins (warm-up)

### 1. Pin / unpin formulae · *Small*
**Why:** Hold a formula at its current version; exclude from upgrades.
**Brew:** `brew pin <f>` · `brew unpin <f>` · `brew list --pinned` (source of truth for pinned state).
**Plugs into:**
- `BPHomebrewInterface` — add `pinFormula:withReturnBlock:` / `unpinFormula:` (call `performBrewCommandWithArguments:`), and a `listPinnedFormulae` call.
- `BPHomebrewManager` — add a `pinnedNames` set to the reload flow + `isFormulaPinned:` helper.
- UI — a pin badge (SF Symbol `pin.fill`) in the detail pane/row; "Pin/Unpin Formula" in the Formula + context menus (`MainMenu.xib` → `BPHomebrewViewController` IBAction, target 547).
**TDD-first:** parser test for `brew list --pinned` → `Set<name>`; manager test that `isFormulaPinned:` reflects it; mock returns one pinned fixture (e.g. `mockgit`) → UI presence test for the badge.

### 2. Surface Dependents inline · *Small–Medium* (reframe: the data path already exists)
**Why:** "What depends on this?" is already computed (`brew uses --installed`) but buried in a menu→text-popover. Show it inline in the always-visible detail pane, next to Dependencies/Conflicts.
**Plugs into:**
- `BPSelectedFormulaViewController` (+ `BPSelectedFormula.xib`) — add a "Required by" stack row + label outlet, mirroring the Dependencies row.
- Populate **async** on selection via the existing `dependantsForFormulaName:onlyInstalled:YES` (⚠️ `brew uses` is slowish — fetch off-main + cache per formula; show "None"/"—" when empty).
**TDD-first:** a pure `parseDependents:` helper (`"foo\nbar\n"` → `@[foo,bar]`, `""` → `@[]`); update the mock's `dependantsForFormulaName:` to return a fixture so a UI test can assert the row appears. Keep the existing menu/popover as-is.

---

## M2 — The headliner

### 3. Cask support · *Medium–Large* (phase it)
**Why:** The #1 gap — casks (GUI apps) are a huge share of real `brew` usage. Roughly doubles the app's scope.
**Brew:** `brew list --cask --versions` · `brew casks` (all) · `brew outdated --cask --greedy` · `brew info --cask <t>` · `brew install/uninstall/upgrade --cask <t>`.
**Plugs into:**
- `BPListMode` — `kBPListInstalledCasks`, `kBPListAllCasks` (add `…OutdatedCasks` in phase 3).
- New `BPHomebrewInterfaceListCall` subclasses (args `@[@"list",@"--cask",@"--versions"]`, `@[@"casks"]`).
- `BPHomebrewManager` — `installedCasks` / `allCasks` properties + reload.
- `BPFormula` — add a `BOOL cask` flag; install/uninstall/upgrade/info append `--cask` when set (reuse the existing confirmation **sheets**).
- Sidebar — a "Casks" category (Installed/All), SF Symbol `macwindow`.
**Phases:** ① browse installed + all casks (read-only) → ② install/uninstall/upgrade → ③ outdated casks + cask-specific `brew info` parsing (its format differs from formulae — new fixture).
**TDD-first:** parser tests for the cask list lines (extend `BPHomebrewInterfaceListCallTests`); manager reload test; cask-info parse test with a `caskInfo_*.txt` fixture; mock cask fixtures + a UI navigation test.

---

## M3 — Developer power

### 4. Services (`brew services`) · *Medium*
**Why:** Start/stop/restart background services (postgres, redis, nginx) with live status — devs live in this.
**Brew:** `brew services list --json` · `brew services start|stop|restart <name>`.
**Plugs into:**
- **New `BPService` model** (name, status enum, user) — services aren't formulae, don't shoehorn into `BPFormula`.
- `BPHomebrewInterface` — `servicesList` parsed via **`NSJSONSerialization`** (first JSON path here; existing parsers are line-based) + start/stop/restart methods.
- **Dedicated "Services" tool view** (like Doctor/Update are their own views): a table of Name · Status · User with Start/Stop buttons — cleaner than the formula table.
- Sidebar — "Services" under Tools.
**TDD-first:** `parseServicesJSON:` → `[BPService]` from a fixture (great pure seam); manager reload test; mock returns JSON fixture → UI presence test. MVP = user-level services only (skip sudo).

---

## M4 — Glue

### 5. Preferences window *(prerequisite)* + Background updater · *Medium*
**Why:** Passive "your packages need updating" companion; also unlocks settings the other features want (greedy cask upgrades, analytics opt-out).
**Preferences (build first — none exists today):** `BPPreferencesWindowController` + `registerDefaults` in `applicationDidFinishLaunching:` + un-hide the disabled Preferences menu item. Small, enabling PR.
**Background updater plugs into (app shell — plumbing mostly exists):**
- `BPAppDelegate` — an `NSTimer` (interval from prefs) → `reloadFromInterfaceRebuildingCache:NO` → on `homebrewManagerFinishedUpdating:`, read `outdatedFormulae.count` → dock badge + notification (the `requestUserAttentionWithMessageTitle:` path already exists).
- **New `NSStatusItem`** menu-bar extra (none today): outdated count + "Upgrade All" + "Open Cakebrew" + "Quit".
**TDD-first:** extract pure helpers — `badgeLabelForOutdatedCount:` and `shouldNotifyForCount:previous:` — and unit-test those (the timer/status-item glue is integration, verified via CI build).

---

## Recommended order & why
**M1 (Pin + Dependents-inline)** → warm up on the pattern with two high-daily-value, low-risk wins. **M2 (Casks)** → the transformative one, phased so each phase ships. **M3 (Services)** → self-contained, own model + view. **M4 (Preferences + Background updater)** → ties it together and adds settings.

Every item is one-or-more PRs on the usual 9-step workflow (TDD → CI-as-UI-gate → squash-merge), and each leans on the mock (`-BPMockBrew`) so the logic is unit-tested without real Homebrew.

Want me to kick off **M1 with Pin/unpin (C)** — write the failing parser test first and build it out? Or would you like this as a shareable artifact first?

**M1 is complete** — [PR #44](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/pull/44) merged, `main` at `c014564`.

## M1 shipped (6 PRs, #40–#44 + the hotfix)

**Pin/unpin (feature C):**
- `#40` — pinned-state layer (`brew list --pinned` parser, `pinnedFormulae`, `isFormulaPinned:`) — TDD'd
- `#41` — pin/unpin actions + Formula-menu items
- `#42` — EXC_BAD_ACCESS hotfix (nil return block) + regression test
- `#44` — detail-pane "Pinned:" indicator (hidden unless pinned) + right-click context-menu items

**Dependents-inline (the reframed feature):**
- `#43` — "Required by" row in the detail pane (`brew uses --installed`, async + debounced) — TDD'd parser

Every PR: TDD where there's logic, 0 warnings, CI green with the UI Tests job validating each xib at runtime. Net effect — you can now pin/unpin a formula from the menu **or** right-click, see a **Pinned** badge and a **Required by** list in the detail pane, and the earlier crash is fixed with a test guarding it.

## Where things stand
The M1 milestone from the roadmap is done. Remaining roadmap:
- **M2 — Cask support** (the big one — installed/all casks, `install --cask`, etc.)
- **M3 — Services** (`brew services`)
- **M4 — Preferences + background updater**

Two housekeeping notes I'd flag before moving on:
- **Please pull `main`, rebuild, and click Pin end-to-end** — #42 fixed the crash, and now the Pinned badge + context menu should all work; good to confirm on real brew.
- The **`git push` hang** recurred on essentially every push this session (commit lands, retry succeeds). If it keeps happening it's worth checking your network/credential-helper setup — it's costing ~90s per push.

Want to kick off **M2 (Casks)** next, or pause here? Given Casks is the largest item, I'd start by scaffolding the read-only "Casks" sidebar sections (browse installed/all) before wiring operations — but that's a fresh, sizable arc, so a good spot to check in first.

content.text:
